requested.title: Validated BYOK endpoint is later used through unpinned requests

parsedVerdicts.reasoning: The finding remains exploitable in the current code. An authenticated user can register the `generic` cloud provider through `POST /api/account/ai-keys`; the route requires authentication and rejects a declared foreign Origin, but those controls do not constrain a malicious authenticated account. It validates the submitted custom URL with `assertPublicHttpUrl`, and `getUserByok` repeats that validation for each use, but both calls discard the returned `ValidatedTarget.address` and retain only the hostname-bearing URL string. `probeByokKey` subsequently calls ordinary `fetch` on `${baseUrl}/models`, while `fetchAiChat` calls ordinary `fetch` on `${baseUrl}/chat/completions`; the agent LLM proxy, embeddings client, and transcription helper likewise use the resolved custom base URL with ordinary fetches. A controlled hostname can resolve to only public addresses during `assertPublicHttpUrl` and then resolve to an internal address for the separate fetch lookup, so the private-address check does not govern the socket actually opened. The attacker can make the registration probe return a successful public response to obtain `validated_at`, then trigger an enabled BYOK AI surface while rebinding DNS; no application credential is added to the request, but the server performs attacker-directed authenticated POSTs with attacker-controlled request content and processes the resulting response. `safe-fetch.ts` and `pinned-request.ts` implement the necessary DNS pinning, but neither is used on these BYOK request paths. Git history shows that commit `c3e2b4e8` added registration-time and per-use validation for MIN-341, whereas the current `e0da16d0` changes are prose-only; no subsequent change routes these requests through a pinned client.
